item.title: Oil prices back up as U.S. and Iran trade threats to expand 7-month war
item.description: As Iran responds to Trump's threat of annihilation with its own warning of a possible "new front" in the war, global oil prices are rising again.

item.title: Man wounded during 2024 Trump rally shooting in Butler County dies
item.description: One of the men who was wounded in the 2024 attempted assassination of President Trump in Butler, Pennsylvania, has died.

item.title: Banned news outlets back in the White House after judge order and chaotic morning locked out
item.description: CNN, Politico and MS NOW regained access to the White House after a judge's order blocked President Trump's ban. During the morning hours, access was still being denied. CBS News' Ed O'Keefe explains.

item.title: Israel's Netanyahu addresses U.N. as many leaders walk out
item.description: Benjamin Netanyahu is focusing on Iran, and on defending Israel's actions in Gaza and the West Bank amid condemnation from fellow leaders at the U.N.

item.title: Trump hosting China's Xi at White House with AI and tariffs on the agenda
item.description: President Trump is hosting Chinese President Xi Jinping for meetings and a state dinner on Thursday, as the world's two most powerful countries try to extend a tariff truce and grapple with a rivalry on advanced AI.

item.title: Mortgage rates are back above 7%. How much higher could they climb?
item.description: Rates are "far more likely to go up than down by the end of the year," a senior economist at Realtor.com told CBS News.

item.title: Former U.S. ambassador to China says he fears Trump may be taking soft approach with Xi Jinping
item.description: Nicholas Burns, the former U.S. ambassador to China, joins CBS News with his take on the Trump-Xi summit and on diplomatic relations with the U.S. adversary.

item.title: Parts of key U.S. military equipment may be in China's hands
item.description: China may have its hands on some parts of the most powerful American fighter jets. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata reports.

item.title: First known hack by rogue AI agent of government website
item.description: Australia says an OpenAI model hacked a government website containing health information. CBS News' Jo Ling Kent reports.

item.title: Journalists regain access to White House after judge blocks Trump's media ban
item.description: Reporters whose White House access was revoked were allowed to enter the complex again, hours after a judge ordered the Trump administration to restore their press credentials.

item.title: MS NOW and CNN reporters regain access to White House after judge's order
item.description: Footage appears to show MS NOW and CNN reporters back inside the White House after a federal judge's order temporarily blocking a Trump administration ban. The journalists were denied access earlier in the day. CBS News' Nancy Cordes reports.

item.title: Hurricane Polo is a powerful Category 4 storm off Mexico. See its path.
item.description: Hurricane Polo's intensity fluctuated between Category 4 and Category 5 — the strongest on the hurricane scale — off Mexico's southwestern coast. Here's the latest on its path.

item.title: Key F-35 missing fighter jet parts may be in China's hands
item.description: There are reports that a shipment of missing F-35 parts ended up in China's hands. The details are emerging as President Trump meets with China's Xi Jinping. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata reports.

item.title: Pandas coming back to Zoo Atlanta for first time since 2024
item.description: During a meeting at the White House, Chinese President Xi Jinping announced that two pandas will be coming to Zoo Atlanta, the first at the zoo since 2024.

item.title: Here's how CBS News covered the Trump-Xi meeting without TV pool coverage amid White House ban
item.description: The White House continued to ban several news outlets despite a federal judge's order to temporarily restore access. This comes amid a vital meeting between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington, D.C. Here's our coverage of the events without access to the television pool usually staffed by five networks.

item.title: Conductor Gustavo Dudamel in 2010 | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: This month marks the debut of Gustavo Dudamel as the new musical director of the New York Philharmonic. In 2010, Bob Simon visited the then-29-year-old conductor and product of El Sistema, Venezuela's radical approach to music education as he led the Los Angeles Philharmonic.

item.title: U.K. prime minister teases possible return of booze to soccer matches
item.description: British leader and soccer fan Andy Burnham told reporters a four-decade ban on alcohol in stadium bleachers at men's games is "discrimination."

item.title: Six Flags coaster accused of causing dozens of brain injuries
item.description: A roller coaster at a Six Flags amusement park in California caused over 100 injuries to riders, new lawsuits claim. Six Flags declined to comment on pending litigation. CBS News' Carter Evans reports.

item.title: Huge waves and high tides flood coastal areas as nor'easter threatens the East Coast
item.description: A powerful nor'easter is causing huge waves and flooding some parts of the East Coast. CBS News' Rob Marciano and Jessica Burch have the forecast.

item.title: Trump meets with China's Xi as media outlets suspend pool coverage
item.description: President Trump welcomed China's President Xi Jinping to the White House for a political summit. This comes as the White House television pool continues to protest a ban on several outlets. CBS News' Nancy Cordes explains.

item.title: Hawaii under another hurricane watch as new storm closes in
item.description: Nolo is expected to become a hurricane sometime Thursday and could become a major hurricane by the weekend as it approaches Hawaii's Big Island.

item.title: Sylvester Stallone jokes about one of his wildest jobs before fame
item.description: Sylvester Stallone said he took a series of odd jobs to make ends meet before the bruised but unbowed Rocky Balboa.

item.title: Sylvester Stallone jokes about cleaning lion cages at the Central Park Zoo before fame
item.description: Sylvester Stallone took on a series of odd jobs to make ends meet before becoming a Hollywood legend. He tells correspondent Tracy Smith about one of his wildest gigs. Watch more of their conversation this weekend on "CBS Sunday Morning."

item.title: Will an FDA crackdown curb access to cheaper GLP-1 weight-loss drugs?
item.description: The FDA has warned a major compounding pharmacy that it violated federal law by making copies of blockbuster weight-loss drugs in "inordinate amounts."

item.title: Farmers consider backing other politicians as they struggle to make a living
item.description: Iowa farmers are awaiting relief news as President Trump meets with China's Xi Jinping. Meanwhile, some are reconsidering their political backing while inflation impacts their crops. CBS News' Lana Zak reports.

item.title: Marineland dolphin dies at Spain aquarium in latest death after rescue
item.description: Echo, one of four dolphins transferred to Oceanogràfic València from Marineland Canada, died on Wednesday, the Spanish facility said.

item.title: Taylor Swift to debut "Patient Zero" music video at VMAs. Watch a preview.
item.description: Taylor Swift announced her new single "Patient Zero" earlier this week, saying she has been "impatiently waiting" to announce that it will be out on Friday.

item.title: Wastin' Away Again in Margaritaville… With No Estate Plan?! | Money Moves with Jill Schlesinger
item.description: Why are Jill and Mark doing a deep dive on Margaritaville? Well, three years have passed since Jimmy Buffett died, and his family is still fighting over a $275 million estate. In today's episode, Jill and Mark explain why estate planning is essential and why you don't need to be rich to need a trust. Plus, how did caller Sam accumulate $370,000 by age 30 on a $95,000 salary?!

item.title: Dolly Parton's estate granted restraining order against her nephew
item.description: A Tennessee judge granted Dolly Parton's estate a temporary restraining order Wednesday against the late singer's nephew Bryan Seaver and his private security company.

item.title: Trump shares more details on $5,000 dividends in exclusive interview
item.description: CBS News Texas political reporter Jack Fink spoke with President Trump for an exclusive interview during the president's visit to North Texas.
